title: Section-Audit Map
subject: solver-status overclaim and unsupported deployment readiness in a synthetic Results excerpt
eyebrow: Generic IEEE/ACM engineering conventions · venue not specified · teaching fixture
summary: A synthetic Results excerpt describing a 12-instance MILP solve, mapped finding by finding. Each numbered entry preserves the concern layer, identifies the sentence that triggered the finding, and shows the bounded correction supported by the excerpt's own reported solver-status data and the accompanying no-further-evidence note.
footer: Generated by applying the checked-in ieee-acm-paper-writing skill, section-audit mode with the --html-map modifier, to a supplied synthetic Results excerpt. The excerpt and its numbers are synthetic and supplied by the user for this evaluation; no external source was consulted.

findings.title: Universal optimality claim contradicted by the excerpt's own data
findings.source: The optimizer always returns the global optimum within 10 s.
findings.evidence: The next sentence in the same excerpt reports that 3 of the 12 instances reached the 60 s time limit with feasible incumbents and final gaps of 4.1%, 5.3%, and 7.8% rather than a certified optimum. A feasible time-limited incumbent is not a certified optimum.
findings.consequence: The opening sentence asserts an unconditional universal guarantee that the excerpt's own reported results directly contradict for 3 of 12 instances (25%).
findings.correction: Replace the universal claim with the reported, instance-scoped outcome: of 12 instances, 9 terminated with solver status OPTIMAL under a 1% relative MIP-gap tolerance; the remaining 3 reached the 60 s time limit with feasible incumbents and gaps of 4.1%, 5.3%, and 7.8%.

findings.title: Unsupported 10 s timing figure
findings.source: The optimizer always returns the global optimum within 10 s.
findings.evidence: The only timing figure the excerpt supports is the 60 s time limit reached by 3 instances. No per-instance solve time, and no 10 s measurement of any kind, is reported, and the task states that no timing measurements outside these solver logs are supplied.
findings.consequence: The 10 s figure has no traceable source artifact; a reader cannot distinguish it from an invented number.
findings.correction: Remove the unsupported 10 s figure. If per-instance wall-clock times exist in the solver logs, request them as an author query before reporting any specific solve-time number.

findings.title: Real-time deployment readiness exceeds the study
findings.source: The method is therefore ready for real-time deployment.
findings.evidence: The excerpt reports only offline solver-status outcomes for 12 instances against a 60 s time limit. The task states that no deployment experiment, exact-optimality certificate, or timing measurement outside these solver logs is supplied.
findings.consequence: The sentence converts a small, finite, offline batch-solve evaluation into a deployment-readiness guarantee that no supplied evidence establishes, including for the 3 instances that did not reach a certified optimum within the time limit.
findings.correction: Remove the deployment-readiness claim. State only the finite, evaluated result: solver status and gap outcomes for the 12 tested instances under the stated 1% relative MIP-gap tolerance and 60 s time limit, with no claim about real-time operational deployment.
